article.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia wound 73 people, officials say
article.summary: Cairo, Sep 08:More than 70 people were wounded in a wave of Houthi attacks Tuesday on Saudi Arabia, authorities said, a major escalation in the renewed conflict between an important US ally and the Iranian-backed rebels in Yemen.The attacks come after weeks of escalating clashes between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen, which shattered a four-year truce in the country's civil war.Fighting has raged on fronts including Yemen's west coast, with government forces saying they have made territorial gains in the provinces of Hodeida, Taiz and Baydah. The Houthi have also launched attacks on Saudi oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.The attacks early Tuesday hit “civilian and economic facilities” in the Saudi cities of Abha's Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait said Maj Gen. article.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites causes fires
article.summary: ALBAWABA - Saudi Arabia has stated that Houthi attacks on its infrastructure – specifically energy sites – has caused fires in the Kingdom in the early hours of Tuesday; shutting down some critical operations."Several energy sector facilities and installations in the southern region of the kingdom were targeted this morning," the official Saudi Press Agency quoted an energy ministry source as saying."The attacks caused fires at several locations, leading to a temporary halt in some operations", they added.Saudi Arabia condemned the attacks that resulted in 73 wounded on its territory, and vowed that it would "take all necessary measures to defend its sovereignty".The Saudi Foreign Minister called for an "immediate halt to all forms of escalation practiced by this militia," specifically referencing their attacks on shipping through the Bab Al-Mandeb strait.The Houthis are currently launching several ballistic missiles and drones towards southern Saudi Arabia. article.summary: Pakistan on Tuesday strongly condemnedattacks carried out by the Houthisagainst civilian and economic targets in Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.In a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan termed the attacks a “flagrant violation” of the Kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, warning that they pose a threat to regional peace and stability and undermine efforts to secure a durable resolution to the conflict in Yemen.Pakistan reiterated its “unwavering support” for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and prosperity of Saudi Arabia, and expressed complete solidarity with the Kingdom’s leadership, government and people.
